findings.name: QUICK RUN
findings.note: measured at a reduced box and tick count. Good enough to say whether something broke; NOT good enough to quote — a published number is a `full` run.

findings.name: spread over a 12× change in the rate

expect.of: LARGE — with a sink in it, the balance depends on how fast the rule is run
expect.because: f → p + (1−p)f then f(1−p) has the rate cancelling; adding annihilation breaks that, because creation scales with p and destruction scales with density

findings.name: occupancy over (1−p)/(2−p)

expect.of: WELL BELOW 1 — this theory annihilates, and the derivation has no term for it
expect.because: annihilation is a sink f → p + (1−p)f then f(1−p) does not contain, so a theory that destroys cannot sit at the fixed point of one that does not

findings.note: which means the ½ this book quotes as 'the vacuum's derived occupancy' is the occupancy of a medium NEITHER of its theories is — and since every screening length here is a mean free path, that is worth more than a factor of two.

entries.what: sheet emission and isotropic emission give the same falloff, so the approximation every measurement in this book uses is a fair one

findings.name: QUICK RUN
findings.note: measured at a reduced box and tick count. Good enough to say whether something broke; NOT good enough to quote — a published number is a `full` run.

findings.name: worst shape difference

expect.of: small — the same falloff whichever way the source emits
expect.because: the inverse-square law comes from a FIXED number of rays over a shell, and how they are distributed over the shell should not change how it thins

findings.note: normalised at the innermost radius, so this compares the falloff and not the amplitude — a sheet puts out l.SHEET rays a tick against isotropic's l.DEG, so they are not expected to be the same size

findings.name: amplitude ratio, sheet / isotropic
findings.note: l.SHEET / l.DEG = 0.3077 if the two differ only by how many rays go out a tick

entries.what: the reading of what counts as a meeting decides the vacuum's occupancy, and therefore whether any force in this model is measurable at all

findings.name: QUICK RUN
findings.note: measured at a reduced box and tick count. Good enough to say whether something broke; NOT good enough to quote — a published number is a `full` run.

findings.name: readings that resolve an attraction at all

expect.of: more than none — a reading in which no force can be measured is not a reading of this model
expect.because: two bodies drawing together is the one thing every version of this model has agreed on, so it is the test a reading of the rules has to pass

findings.note: strongest: head-on/one at 5.8σ

findings.name: the default reading's attraction

expect.of: positive and resolved — co-located, one meeting a point a tick
expect.because: this is what the article's sentence says: any two rays that arrive together have met, and what is left is A SINGLE neutral point

findings.note: 1.4σ · fill 0.071 · mean free path 14.0 cells

findings.name: what pulsing costs, under the default reading
findings.note: inert -8.60e-1 at 1.4σ against pulsing 1.07e-1 at 0.5σ. A body that pulses spends itself emitting its own rays instead of passing the vacuum's along, which is what being massive costs; a body that does not is carried by what the expansion sends it.

findings.name: spread in occupancy across the four readings
findings.note: how far apart four readings of one sentence put the vacuum — and since every screening length here is 1/fill, this is the factor by which the range of every force in this model depends on a choice nobody had written down
